text: Ordered arrabbiata for a late-night study break; it arrived 80 minutes late and cold. Exams are stressful enough.
raat ko padhai ke beech muffin manga, thoda mash hua aaya par fresh tha. hostel delivery ka yahi scene hai.
Cold brew at 11 pm for a study all-nighter - sealed tight, still icy, chocolatey. My exam-week fuel.
Ninety minutes for one order during exam week. The app kept blaming high demand. Dinner became breakfast.
Chilli cheese toast reached still warm in a snug box at 10 pm. A study-night delivery that actually worked.
Shake came late but thick as promised. Exam-season delay, I suppose - half the hostel ordered together.
Fries arrived warm enough to eat over notes. Not crispy-fresh, but exam week forgives a lot.
Ordered a hot chocolate for a feverish all-nighter; got a melted iced latte instead. Exam week needs better.
Croissant a little squashed in the bag but buttery inside. Midnight study snack, acceptable.
Cheesecake delivered in 30 minutes during the exam rush, chilled and glossy. Best revision break ever.
Two hours for a single dessert order on the night before my exam. Cold, late, and the app refunded nothing.
Waffle arrived with maple on the side so it stayed crisp. Ate it between mock tests - perfect.
Cappuccino for a night of revision arrived stone cold. The foam had collapsed into sad milk.
Cold brew for exam eve, delivered fast and sealed. The orange twist survived. Needed it.
Arrabbiata still warm after a 40-minute ride. Spicy enough to keep me awake through chapter nine.
The whole bag leaked - my notes on the doorstep got coffee stains along with dinner. Disaster before the exam.
Fries and dip packed separately, arrived on time during the exam-week dinner rush. Sensible packing.
Hot chocolate genuinely hot at midnight, marshmallows packed on the side. Exam-week kindness in a cup.
Study-group order of 8 drinks for the library meetup: two cappuccinos short and one unmarked. Chaos.
Fifteen sandwiches for the night-shift team during audit season - labelled, on time, still warm.
Ordered 12 coffees for an exam-prep workshop; six arrived, all wrong. Had to refund the whole thing.
Half the office order arrived in the first bag, the rest 25 minutes later. At least everything matched the list.
Ten muffins for the team, each in its own box with a sticker. One blueberry missing, otherwise clean.
Weekend study-hall order: 14 filter coffees labelled by name and froth intact. Organised.
Bulk fries for the office all arrived cold in one soggy stack. Nobody touched them after five minutes.
team ke liye 12 chai mangayi, aadhi der mein aayi aadhi baad mein. sab sahi thi par meeting late ho gayi.
Eighteen croissants for the quarter-end crunch - layered boxes, none crushed, delivered before standup.
Walked in for 10 cappuccinos before the morning exam review; packed and ready in 12 minutes.
Ordered ahead for pickup, still waited 35 minutes while they made delivery orders. Missed the meeting.
Six lattes to go for the team - one came as a cappuccino and I only noticed back at the office.
Morning coffee took 9 minutes because a laptop crowd held the counter. The drink itself was fine.
Paid 220 for a drink I waited 12 minutes for. The work-from-cafe crowd had every table and all the staff's time.
8:15 am, cappuccino in hand by 8:19 even with exam-week students everywhere. The counter moves.
Croissant and coffee packed flat in the kraft bag, no spills on the metro. Morning done right.
Ten-minute wait for a latte while three staff argued over a delivery ticket. Not commuter-friendly.
Filter coffee to go in six minutes despite the study crowd. Strong decoction, quick hands.
Left without ordering after 15 minutes - my ticket was never even printed. The queue was all laptops.
Espresso ready before I finished paying. The fastest counter in Indiranagar on a Tuesday.
Quick cappuccino at the counter before office; students had the tables but takeaway was instant.
Every table was a laptop and headphones. Drank standing, left fast. Not a cafe on workday mornings.
subah ka espresso 140 mein jaldi mila. table toh nahi mili par counter pe kaam ho gaya.
Cashier took three delivery calls before my payment. Twenty minutes for one shot. Done with mornings here.
office delivery: latte gunguni aayi, foam gayab. garam cheez 40 min travel nahi kar sakti.
Arrived warm-ish, lid secure. Desk coffee on a deadline - did the job, nothing more.
exam week mein yahi adda hai. chai 140, wifi free, aur koi bhagata nahi. teen ghante padhai ho gayi.
fries aur notes - exam combo. par prices thode upar gaye hain, aur plug point ke liye ladai hoti hai.
came to study, found zero seats - every table taken by laptops since morning. turned back home.
kulhad chai achhi thi but exam week mein yahan jagah milna mushkil. aadha time plug dhoondhne mein gaya.
chai aur cheese toast, do dost, ek table, aur syllabus khatam. brew is the unofficial exam hall.
barista bhaiya ne humein do ghante tak nahi chheda, cold brew refill bhi time pe. exam season saviour.
160 ke fries, teen ghante ki seat, unlimited notes review. student budget approved.
muffin leke library bhaaga. 160 mein theek hai par exam week mein queue bhi lambi thi.
raat 11 baje fries mangayi study break ke liye, thandi aayi. padhai ka mood off.
chai ka order hostel pe, aayi toh coffee nikli. exam se pehle ki raat, aur yeh mix-up. bura.
midnight order: cheese toast aur fries dono garam. mess food ke baad yeh toh luxury hai.
strawberry shake thick thi par aate aate melt ho gayi, aur 240 student budget pe heavy pada.
do chai 140 each, garam, kulhad ke baad glass mein bhi mazedaar. all-nighter fuel mil gaya.
croissant mash hoke aaya aur thanda bhi. exam week mein yeh toh aur bura laga.
Fries to the PG arrived crunchy, shared three ways during revision. Value for money, no complaints.
iced latte 260 - padhai ke liye chahiye thi, aayi 50 min mein. taste sahi, pocket crying.
Quiet study-season afternoon: rose latte, cinnamon roll, soft music, and every laptop minding its own business.
Dessert in a hushed corner while students crammed around us. A library with better food.
Hot chocolate on a grey exam-week afternoon; the staff kept the volume low for the studiers. Classy.
Flat white excellent; the room was more co-working space than cafe today. Still lovely.
Muted playlists, laptop glow, grey light through the window. The calmest room in Indiranagar right now.
matcha ke saath quietly baithe, sab padh rahe the. humara brunch bhi shant ho gaya, achha laga.
Brunch good, but whispering through it because half the room is revising is a strange vibe.
Sunday before results - we split a cheesecake and ignored everyone else's exam stress. Bliss.
They gently asked a loud table to keep it down for the exam kids. That is management.
Cheesecake home-delivered for a post-exam treat - glaze intact, box clean, mood restored.
Rose latte arrived fragrant and warm while I pretended to work from home. Self-care via delivery.
Waffle in a box, maple separate, still crisp edges. A weekend brunch without leaving the sofa.
Hot chocolate arrived cool with a loose lid - half of it in the bag. Wasted a cosy plan.
Two hours on one iced latte during exam week; the seat was gold dust but nobody pushed me out.
Cold brew was fine but I circled 15 minutes for a table. Work-from-cafe only works if there is a seat.
Plug, wifi, cold brew, three solid hours of output. The study-season crowd kept the room focused.
They let me camp through a long call without a single glare. Iced latte refilled once. Perfect work spot.
No plugs free, wifi crawling under the exam-week load, and a queue of laptops behind me. Left mid-call.
260 for an iced latte is steep when you stay three hours, but the table and wifi justify it. Barely.
Every two-seater taken by one laptop each. Shared a table, couldn't take calls. Cold brew deserved better.
Matcha and a working morning - wifi held, nobody hovered for the table. Exam season has a quiet etiquette here.
Meera nudged me toward the corner with the plug before I even asked. Three hours, zero interruptions.
Laptop city today. Managed two hours wedged between a study group and a loud call. Drink was good though.
do cold brew, chaar ghante kaam, wifi solid. 500 rupaye mein office se sasta co-working mila.
The drink was great, but at exam time you pay 220 and gamble on whether a seat exists. Today I got lucky.
Kids' pasta dinner surrounded by silent studying students - we were the loud ones. Wait was long too.
bachchon ke saath aaye par pura cafe padh raha tha. halka sa awkward, par staff ne adjust karwaya.
Dev made the arrabbiata gentle for the kids even during the evening rush. Pasta night saved.
They found us the corner table away from the study crowd and the shakes came fast. Smooth evening.
bachche bhookhe, khana 45 min, aur har taraf padhai chal rahi thi. family ke liye theek nahi abhi.
Post-exam treat for my daughter: waffle, shake, and a team that cheered her result. Sweet people.
Kids' post-exam feast delivered: fries crisp, shakes thick, everything sealed. Celebration sorted.
Promised the kids pasta after the exam; it arrived an hour late and cold. The celebration flopped.
Kids' dinner arrived warm enough and packed tight. Kids ate, parents relieved.
Kids' study-break order arrived - no spills, right items, twenty minutes flat.
Waffle a bit soft on arrival but the kids finished it. Exam-season delivery, acceptable.
bachchon ki hot chocolate late aur gunguni aayi. unhone doodh hi pee liya. meh.
Cheesecake slice for the exam-finisher arrived perfect - chilled, unbroken, gone in two minutes.
Found a cafe full of students studying over filter coffee. Quietest, most focused room I have sat in.
Rose milk while Bengaluru's students crammed around me. Felt like peeking into real local life.
Kulhad chai in a pink cafe during exam season - half library, half cafe, completely charming.
Matcha fine, but the cafe was one big study hall. Nice to look at, hard to relax in.
The barista explained the dabarah froth even with a queue of anxious students behind me. Lovely people.
Came for a slow brunch; found a silent exam-cram hall where my conversation got glares. Wrong week.
Cold brew among a sea of laptops and flashcards. Odd energy, great coffee.
Chai and filter coffee back to back - both outstanding. Even the stressed students were friendly.
Rose milk for 180, a seat by the pastry fridge, and a free show of exam-season intensity. Worth it.
A pastry grabbed between sightseeing stops; the counter was busy with students but service stayed quick.
Mine, same time every morning, out before I finish saying hi. Exam crowd changes nothing.
Cappuccino to go while the tables fill with students - five minutes, sealed lid, done.
In and out in four minutes even with the exam-week morning line. The counter never slips.
subah ki line exam-week mein lambi ho gayi hai. mera usual toh waisa hi hai, bas thoda aur wait.
Fifteen minutes behind a wall of student orders; my ticket got buried. Even regulars queue in exam week.
Zoya had my filter coffee started before I reached the counter. Years of mornings, memorised.
Kabir asked about my daughter's exams and had my cappuccino started before I ordered. This is why I keep coming.
exam week mein table milna mushkil, aur mera usual bhi thoda mehenga. par jaana band nahi kiya.
Even with students camping everywhere, they kept my corner free till 9. That is how you keep a regular.
Flat white unchanged through the exam rush. Price nudged up ten rupees - noticed, accepted.
Evening chai in a room full of studiers. Meera still found me a seat and a smile.
exam week ne mera quiet adda coaching centre bana diya, laptops ki line lagi hui. coffee abhi bhi sahi hai.
